title: Poxabog / Poxabogue Pond
summary: Poxabogue preserves an Indigenous pond name in Sagaponack, connecting changing water levels with the language recorded in Southampton’s colonial land surveys.
map_geometry_source: Modern pond reference: OSM relation 13034867. No historical territorial boundary inferred.
why_this_matters: A pond’s changing shoreline can help us understand why a place name mattered. Poxabogue links an Indigenous name preserved in land records with a wetland landscape people can still learn from today.
introduction_title: A Place Name Connected to Water
introduction_content: Poxabog names both a pond and a surrounding farming district in William Wallace Tooker’s 1911 account. He traces forms of the name to Southampton’s 1712 South Division survey, where the pond helped orient surveyors along the East Hampton path. The record shows an Indigenous name continuing to organize the landscape as colonial authorities divided land.1
history_content: The survey spellings include Paugasaboug and Paugaseboug. Tooker also records Pogaseboge in 1724, Pougosoboug in 1726, and Poxabogue in 1763. These are written variants preserved by record keepers, not evidence that the place began with the first surviving mention.1
translation_content: Tooker interpreted the name as a pond that opens out or widens. He related that reading to water levels that fell in dry weather and rose enough in wet periods to flow toward Sagg Swamp and Pond. This is his historical interpretation, rather than a verified modern community pronunciation or translation.1
preservation_content: Suffolk County’s 26-acre park protects land on the pond’s north side. The county describes it as an early-1970s preservation purchase supporting the coastal plain pond ecosystem. A half-mile trail passes through grassland, woods and wetlands to a viewing blind.2
whereintheworld_content:
The dot identifies modern Poxabogue Pond in Sagaponack, south of Little Poxabogue Pond. It does not mark the boundary of the historical farming district or a settlement.3

For public access, use Poxabogue County Park at 191 Old Farm Road, Bridgehampton, and follow posted trail rules. The pond marker is not a trail entrance.2
